newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's BHP winds down steel plant.
newsitem.headline: Australia's BHP winds down steel plant.

text.p: Australian metals and mining giant The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd (BHP) said on Tuesday it would phase out steelmaking at its major Newcastle plant north of Sydney by the end of 1999.
The company, Australia's largest, also said it planned to close its Geelong rod mill and Sydney wire mill in 1999.
Based on a review of domestic and international steel operations, BHP said it would disband its international steel division and restructure BHP Steel around four divisions.

The company did not say how many jobs would be lost, but trade unions in Newcastle -- a traditional industrial centre named after the English industrial city -- have said 2,000 jobs could disappear from the plant and another 1,000 related jobs.

Unlike its British cousin, which has also lost thousands of secondary-industry jobs, Australia's Newcastle will retain a vast coal export industry. BHP said some of its other operations in Newcastle would be expanded.
But the closure is a blow for a country that has been trying for decades to move away from selling raw materials and into downstream processing.
"Australia can't be content with just being an iron ore supplier to our trading partners," Labor Opposition Industry Minister Simon Crean told Reuters.
The plant, built during World War One but updated many times since, was one of Australia's first steps towards downstream minerals processing.
But BHP said the international competition was too tough for the Newcastle plant, which produces two million tonnes a year.
A year-long review had confirmed that world steel prices would continue to fall in an intensely competitive international industry now exploiting cheaper technology.
"I especially regret the need to close steelmaking at Newcastle," said Ron McNeilly, head of BHP steel division.
"Newcastle was the company's entry point to steelmaking and the foundation from which we built our presence in the industry."
